title: DSH Skin Manifest v2
description: Declarative manifest for a dsh-web skin asset directory. Skins are pure assets; the skin-center package is the only loader/renderer. Validators must use this local schema copy and never fetch the $id URL.

skinManifestVersion.description: Manifest file-structure version only; NOT a compatibility negotiation axis (hooks runtime compatibility uses facets.client.apiVersion).

id.description: Globally unique lowercase short id. The skin-center owns scoping under html[data-dsh-skin="<id>"].

license.description: Optional SPDX / license name for third-party artwork.

attribution.description: Optional attribution line shown in the shop.

optional.description: When true, a missing contract follows the declared degradation path (e.g. run without hooks) instead of failing activation.

stylesheet.description: L1 token + L2 semantic styles; scoped under html[data-dsh-skin] by the loader.

patches.description: Optional L3 free-selector patches. High sensitivity; disclosed in the Skin Center UI and the shop.

backgroundMedia.description: Fills the fixed decoration layer 'background'. Wallpaper-Engine wallpaper always wins over this; user manual background wins over it too.

entry.description: hooks.mjs escape-hatch entry. Trusted code, same-review same-release; high sensitivity; NOT the default entry for future out-of-repo extensions.

apiVersion.description: Hooks runtime contract version, independent of skinManifestVersion.

package.description: DEPRECATED v1 field (npm package name). Ignored with a migration warning; never triggers fail-closed.

wiring.description: DEPRECATED v1 field (cordis wiring). Ignored with a migration warning; never triggers fail-closed.

bodyAttr.description: DEPRECATED v1 field (skin-managed body attribute). Scoping is skin-center owned via html[data-dsh-skin]; ignored with a migration warning.

relPath.description: Relative path inside the skin directory: no leading slash, no '..', no protocol URLs.

scrim.description: CSS background shorthand layered over the media for readability.
